concern_details.detail: main architectural components and their responsibilities
concern_details.why: Six components that match the code: Boundary (10 Swing GUIs), Control (10 controllers, with SystemServicesController as the facade), Entity split into services (ReportService, UserService) and entities, Database (PersistenceService, JpaUtil), and the MySQL reports_db from persistence.xml. Each box now gives a one-line responsibility.

Each box names its layer and the Java package behind it (Presentation/Boundary, Application/Control, Domain, Persistence/Database), and the dependency chain runs strictly downward. The note says that Domain Services and Domain Entities are a logical split of the single package Entity, which matches the code (ReportService.java and UserService.java are in Entity). Layer packages would make the layers visible at a glance, but at overview level the box text is enough.

Checked against the imports. The GUIs import only Control.SystemServicesController, plus Control.UserLoginController in UserLoginGUI. The controllers import only Entity.ReportService/UserService, plus ReportCategory. Only ReportService and UserService import Database.PersistenceService, and PersistenceService imports no Entity class. The one direct dependency from controllers to entities (ReportCreationController.java:3, ReportCategory) appears only in the note, not as an edge. That is a small inconsistency, because the identical UI dependency is drawn as an edge.

concern_details.detail: separation of user interface, application logic, domain entities and persistence, and how they collaborate
concern_details.why: The note covers how the layers collaborate: UI and controllers exchange Map<String,Object> data, the facade is the entry point and only login bypasses it, and ReportCategory is the only entity type that reaches the UI and the controllers. The 'ORM mapping' label shows that persistence is tied to the entities through JPA configuration, not through code imports. The code bears all of this out.

level_why: Six components and seven dependencies fit an overview for an architect. The screens, use-case controllers, state classes and enums are merged correctly, and the only finer element (the ReportCategory edge) is there because it is the one place where the layering leaks. Nothing should be cut. Adding layer packages, a provided interface or the individual controllers would take the view past the overview level.
unsupported: pers ..> ent 'ORM mapping' is drawn as a dependency, but the code has no compile-time dependency: PersistenceService is generic over Class<T> and imports no Entity class. The link exists only at runtime, through the <class> list in META-INF/persistence.xml. The label makes this clear enough, so it is acceptable, though the note could also say it is configuration, not code.
missing: The Application Controllers to Domain Entities dependency (ReportCategory, Control/ReportCreationController.java:3) is only in the note. For consistency with the drawn UI-to-entities edge, either draw it or leave both in the note. This is minor.
uml: The notation is acceptable: component elements, dashed dependencies with open arrowheads, and no non-standard stereotypes. Optionally, the external MySQL database could carry a standard keyword (for example «component» is implicit), or it could be shown as an external component. No change is required.
The 'Persistence Layer / Persistence layer (Database)' box text repeats the name. This is a wording issue, not a notation error.
fixes: Optional: make the ReportCategory dependency consistent by drawing ctrl ..> ent as an edge or by moving the ui ..> ent edge into the note.
Optional: in the note, say that the persistence-to-entities link is through JPA configuration (persistence.xml), not code imports.
Optional: remove the repeated 'Persistence layer' wording in the persistence box.
